title: Telemetry Rhythm Deterioration
scenario: A 70-year-old client admitted with chest pain is on continuous cardiac monitoring. The nurse reviews the telemetry flowsheet documenting rhythm and hemodynamic changes across the shift.

tabs.title: Telemetry Flowsheet
rows: Frequent multifocal PVCs, short runs of VT

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Reviewing the full telemetry trend, how should the nurse interpret the rhythm progression?

options.text: The rhythm is progressing from isolated ectopy to sustained ventricular tachycardia with hemodynamic compromise
The changes reflect a stable sinus tachycardia from anxiety
The trend shows resolving atrial fibrillation with a controlled rate
The rhythm indicates a first-degree AV block of no clinical significance

questions.rationale: Isolated PVCs advancing to frequent multifocal PVCs, then short VT runs, and finally sustained VT with a falling blood pressure and symptoms represents a deteriorating, hemodynamically significant ventricular dysrhythmia.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Given the rhythm at 14:00, which action should the nurse take first?

options.text: Assess the client and activate the rapid response / code team
Continue routine monitoring and recheck in one hour
Encourage the client to perform a vagal maneuver
Document the rhythm and wait for the next scheduled rounds

questions.rationale: Sustained ventricular tachycardia with hypotension and near-syncope is unstable and life-threatening, so the nurse immediately assesses the client and summons emergency help rather than delaying or attempting a vagal maneuver.
